entity.name: Saksham Jaiswal
entity.description: Prismio is an independent, open-source systems programming language and compiler project created and maintained by Saksham Jaiswal. It provides a statically typed language that compiles to native machine code through LLVM, with an Adaptive Inference Framework (AIF) for explainable memory placement, direct C interoperability, and a self-hosted compiler toolchain.

projects.name: Prismio
projects.description: Prismio is an open-source, self-hosted systems programming language and compiler that combines modern static language features with explicit systems-level control. It compiles to native code through LLVM, provides direct C ABI interoperability, and uses its Adaptive Inference Framework (AIF) to analyze and explain memory placement and ownership decisions. The project includes a native compiler, standard library, runtime verification tooling, project/build tooling, benchmarks, and developer documentation.

plans.name: Prismio Development Grant 2026
plans.description: The requested ₹6,00,000 will support a 12-month development period focused on expanding and hardening Prismio into a more complete, production-oriented systems programming ecosystem. ₹1,50,000 will support core compiler, language, and LLVM backend development; ₹1,25,000 will support AIF, memory-layout analysis, allocation behavior, and compiler optimizations; ₹1,00,000 will support networking, asynchronous I/O, concurrency primitives, and related standard-library infrastructure; ₹75,000 will support specialized optimization and benchmarking for quantitative finance and low-latency workloads, including predictable latency, data-oriented execution, memory efficiency, and high-throughput numerical and market-data processing; ₹50,000 will support developer tooling, testing, CI, and release infrastructure; and ₹50,000 will support documentation, examples, contributor onboarding, and ecosystem development. The work will result in measurable improvements to the compiler, standard library, runtime, tooling, performance, and contributor experience, with development progress and relevant results made available through the open-source project.
